remaining_gaps.rule: Presence repositioning is permitted before Presence tracks are empty.
remaining_gaps.question: A Spirit still has Presence disks on its Presence tracks. When resolving an ordinary Add Presence instruction, may it choose to reposition one of its Presence already on the island instead of taking a track disk, or is repositioning permitted only after its tracks are empty?
remaining_gaps.predetermined_answer: It may reposition an existing island Presence instead of taking a track disk even while track disks remain. Empty tracks are not a prerequisite. Choose a normally legal destination using existing Presence, then take an own island disk; this does not uncover a new track benefit.

sources.quotation:
If all my Presence from my Spirit Panel is placed on the board, how do I add more?
(.7w4g8oc)
Whenever adding Presence, instead of taking from your Presence Tracks you can use Presence (of yours) already on the island instead.
[sidebar, p. 14]
. You can take it out of any land, including the land you're measuring Range from.
While this option is most often relevant if your Presence tracks are empty, it's not a requirement for doing so.
You cannot place destroyed Presence unless an effect explicitly says so.
(
Discussion elsewhere
(https://www.boardgamegeek.com/thread/1812827/can-presence-tokens-killed-blight-return-game-can)
)

remaining_gaps.why_current_actual_prompts_do_not_reques: Q03 expressly stipulates no Presence on tracks, so cannot distinguish a mistaken only-when-empty restriction. Q36 assumes Add Presence using an island disk and asks measurement/classification and distance of the picked-up disk; it never asks when that substitution is available. Q02 asks which track disks to take, Q24 asks mandatory/impossible instructions and costs, and Q124 asks selecting an entire Growth option. A respondent can answer every requested fact in those prompts while falsely prohibiting repositioning before tracks empty. The broad growth-reposition map row asserts this permission but its question links do not actually request it.
remaining_gaps.novelty: An explicitly published permission branch with a false restriction that survives the existing prompts; not a new location, number, or empty-supply arithmetic example.

remaining_gaps.rule: Dread Apparitions counts direct Power Fear and Bringer nightmare Fear, but excludes ordinary Fear from destroying buildings.
remaining_gaps.question: Dread Apparitions has already resolved in a land. A normal Spirit Power there generates 1 printed Fear and destroys one Town, generating another 1 Fear. How much Defend does Dread Apparitions add? Separately, Bringer’s Power there generates exactly 2 Fear from To Dream a Thousand Deaths pretend-destroying a Town and no other Fear. Does that Fear count, and how much Defend is added?
remaining_gaps.predetermined_answer: The normal Power adds Defend 1, not 2: its printed Fear counts but ordinary Town-destruction Fear does not. The 2 Fear from To Dream a Thousand Deaths does count and adds Defend 2.

remaining_gaps.rule: Tidal Boon supplies an optional rescue from Drowning to any Coastal land for Dahan pushed by that use.
remaining_gaps.question: Ocean uses Tidal Boon on another Spirit, and that Spirit uses this Power’s Push to send a Dahan into Ocean’s active Ocean. May Ocean instead move that Dahan to a nonadjacent Coastal land rather than Drowning it? Who chooses, and is taking that alternative mandatory?
remaining_gaps.predetermined_answer: Yes. The Spirit using Tidal Boon (Ocean) may move that Dahan to any Coastal land instead of Drowning it; the destination need not be adjacent. This is optional. If the option is not taken, the ordinary Ocean Drowning applies. It applies to this Power’s Push, not later unrelated Pushes.

sources.transcribed_passage: If Dahan are pushed to your Ocean, you may move them to any Coastal land instead of Drowning them.

remaining_gaps.why_current_actual_prompts_do_not_reques: Q68 asks whether Tidal Boon can Push from a land without a Town and whether its conditional applies to later unrelated Pushes. It never asks what that conditional permits. Q77-Q80 ask ordinary Drowning and Ocean expiration; Q113 asks the different failed-destruction Push, which is mandatory and adjacent, rather than Tidal’s optional move to any Coastal land. Q35’s general same-land Move permission does not establish this exception to Drowning.
remaining_gaps.novelty: The printed core rescue exception changes the outcome and choice/destination procedure, rather than merely recombining normal Drown and Push rules.

remaining_gaps.rule: Explicit threshold timing words can place effects before earlier-printed base instructions.
remaining_gaps.question: Wrap in Wings of Sunlight meets its threshold. Its target land initially has no Dahan, but Dahan are available in adjacent lands. Does its threshold’s “First, Gather up to 3 Dahan” happen before the base Move, so those Dahan can then be moved and the destination Defended, or must the base Move finish first because it is printed higher? Likewise, with Dissolve the Bonds of Kinship’s threshold, does its Invader-on-Invader Damage happen before or after Pushing the Explorers?
remaining_gaps.predetermined_answer: Wrap’s explicit First instruction Gathers before the base Move, allowing those gathered Dahan to be moved by the base effect and Defend 5 in the destination if at least one moves. Dissolve’s explicit Before Pushing instruction resolves its threshold Damage before the Explorer Push (after the preceding replacements). Such timing words override the default top-to-bottom position; they do not create another Power use.

remaining_gaps.why_current_actual_prompts_do_not_reques: Q15 asks multiple threshold/Power Element use, targets, use count and Instead. Q27 asks Elements gained/lost while a Power resolves; Q16 asks possible/impossible mandatory instructions. These do not request the exception for an explicitly earlier-timed threshold. Q61 asks Dissolve’s missing symbol and simultaneity of the Damage, not its timing relative to Push. Q63 asks Wrap’s zero-movement/Defend dependency and same-land Move, without any met threshold or First instruction. A mistaken always-resolve-all-base-text-before-thresholds rule survives those actual prompts.
remaining_gaps.novelty: One explicit temporal exception to the default order, illustrated by two original-core card faces; not two separate additions and not a cosmetic substitution of card names.
